test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the significance of the NVS-02 satellite launched in 2025?

options.text: It will enhance India's regional navigation capabilities.
It will conduct scientific experiments in space.
It will provide weather forecasting services.
It will provide communication services to rural areas.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It will enhance India's regional navigation capabilities.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NVS-02** is a satellite designed as part of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), also known as NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation).
 
• The satellite will significantly enhance **India's regional navigation capabilities**, enabling accurate positioning services over the Indian subcontinent and surrounding regions.
 
• NavIC is India's indigenous alternative to GPS (Global Positioning System), designed to support **civilian, military, and commercial applications**.
 
• The NVS-02 satellite will augment the existing constellation of NavIC satellites, ensuring better accuracy, coverage, and reliability for navigation services.
 
• It is equipped with advanced payloads, including L1, L5, and S-band signals, to improve positioning accuracy for users across diverse sectors like transportation, agriculture, and disaster management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS)**

 
 
• IRNSS, operationally known as NavIC, is an independent regional navigation satellite system developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
 
• NavIC provides positioning services with an accuracy of up to 20 meters over India and a range of 1,500 kilometers beyond its borders.
 
• It serves both civilian and military users, with applications in navigation, fleet management, disaster warning, and more.
 
 
 
• **NavIC vs GPS**
 
 
• While GPS is a global navigation system operated by the US, NavIC is a regional system focused on India and nearby regions.
 
• NavIC offers two types of services: the Standard Positioning Service (SPS) for civilian users and the Restricted Service (RS) for military and strategic applications.
 
 
 
• **Payload Features**
 
 
• The NVS-02 satellite carries dual-frequency (L5 and S-band) signals, which reduce errors caused by ionospheric disturbances.
 
• These signals enable improved accuracy and are critical for applications like aviation, maritime navigation, and precision farming.
 
 
 
• **Significance of NavIC**
 
 
• NavIC is crucial for India's strategic autonomy, reducing dependency on foreign navigation systems like GPS.
 
• It supports various sectors, including transportation, fisheries, defense, and disaster management, enhancing India's technological self-reliance.
